title: Cross-container write pacing without shared storage: measure the shared `x-ratelimit-used` counter as the fleet gate's cross-container signal; the per-container conservative profile is the knob until then
body:
## What holds, and what does not

`scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs` (with #19641 / #19642) serialises every write verb behind one lease, spaces them, and raises the gap for an announced batch — **within one filesystem**. On a host where every session shares a home that is the whole fleet on that host; inside one cloud container it covers a PM seat and every subagent it fans out into worktrees — which is exactly the shape of the second restriction (17 cards in 29 s from one seat's fan-out, each process pacing itself).

Across containers nothing is shared: each container holds its own lease, its own budget and its own installation token. The maintainer has confirmed there is **no shared volume** to mount into the cloud containers, so pointing `OS_PM_WRITE_PACE_FILE` at one is not available. This card is the follow-up that decision leaves open.

## The three routes, with their costs

- **A — per-container conservative profile.** No coordination: raise each container's minimum gap to 1.5 s × the maximum number of concurrently writing seats (seven lanes → about 10 s) and divide the hourly budget by the same number. Zero new mechanism — the existing `OS_PM_WRITE_MIN_GAP_MS` / `OS_PM_WRITE_HOURLY_MAX` overrides carry it (their header currently calls them test-only; adopting them as a *profile* is a one-paragraph contract change). Cost: every seat is slowed even when alone, and it cannot stop N containers issuing in the same instant.
- **B — a lock ref on GitHub.** `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/git/refs` (`refs/locks/fleet-write`) is atomic — 422 when it exists — and `DELETE` releases. Cost: two extra write requests per content write against the platform's ~500 content-generating requests per hour, plus a TTL story for a container that dies holding it. Not recommended.
- **C — adaptive pacing from the platform's own shared counter.** Every response to an installation token carries `x-ratelimit-used` / `x-ratelimit-remaining` for the **installation's** bucket, and every container of this fleet draws on that one bucket. Between two consecutive requests of its own, a container can read how much the counter moved beyond its own requests — that difference is the other containers' activity, delivered on every response, at zero extra requests. A gate can widen its gap in proportion (a proxy for total request rate, not the write rate alone — the rule has to be measured before it is trusted).

## What this card asks for

1. **Measure C first.** From two cloud sessions running at once: log `x-ratelimit-used` on every response for an hour of ordinary seat work; confirm the counter is shared across containers (it should be — one installation) and how noisy the delta is against a single container's own request count. Write the reading into `write-pace.mjs`'s header, whatever it says.
2. If the signal is usable: rule ⑥ in `write-pace.mjs` — a gap multiplier derived from the observed foreign delta, bounded, printed when it changes, with the batteries a self-test can drive offline (an injected header sequence).
3. Whichever way (1) goes, adopt A's knobs as a declared **profile** rather than test-only overrides, so a cloud environment can carry a conservative setting with one variable.

⛔ Out of scope: any new CI gate or ratchet; a coordination service; a shared volume (ruled out).
